leading_positions.synthesis: Four members prefer a single-achievement prize for optical lattice clocks to Katori and Ye (Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce). They share the reading that the magic-wavelength lattice is a physical idea and not only engineering, that 1e-18 performance has been reproduced across JILA/NIST, RIKEN/Tokyo, SYRTE and PTB, and that the two-name attribution is among the cleanest on the shortlist. They differ in emphasis: Kroll and Lindroth stress the new measurement regime and the science it enables (millimetre redshift, constants, dark matter); Johansson and Pearce also cite breadth of opening support. All four acknowledge the discovery-versus-metrology question and the 2005 and 2012 overlap, and Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce want the citation worded around the lattice clock and not the comb, while Johansson and Kroll want it kept away from the redefinition of the second. Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson, who prefer B019, each name B042 as their first alternative.

Three members prefer a single-achievement prize for magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer (Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson). They share the prediction-then-discovery structure, broad independent reproduction, and a citation limited to the flat-band prediction and the observed phases without claiming the pairing mechanism. They also share the same weaknesses: only eight years since 2018, and the omission of Yuan Cao and other early experimental groups. Mehlig and Olsson moved to this ballot after reading colleagues. Eriksson says B042 is the better-settled discovery if the committee judges the field too young, and Olsson says B042 is the cleaner and more mature alternative.

One member (Danielsson) prefers a two-person IceCube prize to Halzen and Spiering, after moving his first place from the Higgs experiments (B057) because of the attribution problem for the ATLAS and CMS leaders. He argues that the diffuse astrophysical flux is secure and that the citation should rest on it and on the telescopes, not on 3-4 sigma source identifications. Pearce lists B032 as his first alternative, though his round-1 configuration is B042. Others raise doubts about pioneer credit (AMANDA, Baikal, DUMAND) and about interpretive maturity.

areas_of_agreement: All eight round-1 configurations are single-achievement prizes with one ballot ID; no member proposes a multi-part prize, although Eriksson raises a two-part pairing of B019 with a more mature candidate as an open question.

B042 and B019 are the mutual fall-backs: Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson (B019) list B042 as their first alternative, and Johansson (first alternative), Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce (alternatives) list B019 among theirs.

Members accept a citation limited to what is established: the lattice-clock concept and its realisation, the flat-band prediction and observed correlated phases, and the diffuse neutrino flux, without claiming explanations or later milestones.

The Higgs experiments (B057) are accepted as major science, but members who discussed them (Danielsson, Olsson, Pearce) say the three credited names are detector leaders and that the obstacle is attribution, not merit. No member prefers B057 in round 1.

B050 and B038 compete for the same Zoller-centred credit and should not be split (Eriksson, Lindroth), and B028 has an attribution gap (Krivanek and the STEM corrector line) that Eriksson, Olsson and Pearce each call serious. Neither is any member's round-1 preference.
KPZ (B037) has no explicit supporter in round 1; its opening advocate (Mehlig) has moved to B019.
scientific_disputes: Whether optical lattice clocks count as a physical discovery about nature (millimetre redshift, constants, dark matter) or as a refinement of a metrology line already recognised in 2005 and 2012. Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson and Pearce read it as the former or sufficiently so; Mehlig and Olsson weigh it nearer to refinement or to an instrument, and Danielsson places a new window on nature above it.

Whether a prize for twisted bilayer graphene can rest on the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting phases while the pairing mechanism and the nature of several correlated states are unresolved. Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson say yes with a narrow citation; Johansson and Danielsson say the open mechanism favours waiting; Kroll asks what is gained by waiting while the clock case is complete.

Whether the diffuse neutrino flux alone is sufficient for B032 while individual sources (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, the Galactic plane) remain at 3-4 sigma, and whether the 2002 neutrino prize is a real obstacle (Danielsson says no; Pearce raised it).

Whether the committee should favour an instrument or enabling-technology prize (B042, B028) over a discovery of a new phase or messenger; Olsson and Danielsson weigh this differently from Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce.
attribution_disputes: B042: all proposers named Katori and Ye, but Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto, Hinkley, Bloom and the NIST, PTB and SYRTE groups are cited by several members as decisive in particular demonstrations. Olsson asks what Ye's record-setting clocks add that is original and not only superior; Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce say Ye's role should be worded as realisation at record accuracy and not as comb work.

B019: the three credited names cover the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction and the Jarillo-Herrero group, but Yuan Cao (first author of the 2018 papers), Dean, Kim, Young, Efetov, Ashoori and the earlier twist-angle theory of Lopes dos Santos and collaborators are cited as possible claims. Mehlig, Eriksson and Olsson differ on whether this can be handled in the citation wording alone.

B032 and B057: Halzen and Spiering are described as a cleaner pair than three ATLAS and CMS leaders, but the AMANDA, Baikal, DUMAND and ANTARES pioneers are not covered. Members who discussed B057 say Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are detector leaders and not the discovery-analysis leaders, so a detector-centred citation would be a different award.

Similar proposals differ in laureates and framing: B050 (Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger, Zoller) and B038 (Cirac, Zoller, Blatt) both centre on Zoller but credit different experimentalists; B049 has four credited names, so a three-person limit would cut a real contributor (Blais or Girvin).
maturity_disputes: B019 is eight years old and the pairing mechanism is unsettled; Johansson and Danielsson would wait a few years, whereas Mehlig, Olsson and Eriksson argue that robust reproduction of the phases suffices if the citation is narrow.

B042 performance is reproduced by independent laboratories now, but the redefinition of the second has not happened. Johansson asks whether to wait for it; Kroll cautions against citing it, since it is a metrological decision and not a physics discovery.
B032 has an established diffuse flux but source identification below 5 sigma, and the field may look different in five years (Danielsson, Pearce, Kroll).

Whether recent prizes in quantum information, superconducting circuits and AMO physics argue against another award in that cluster (B042, B050, B038, B049); Olsson and Johansson raise it, while Kroll and Lindroth say the 2005 and 2012 prizes honoured different contributions.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Chalmers, director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology) discloses that B049 (circuit QED), B051 (optomechanics with superconducting qubits) and B038 (quantum computing foundations) fall in his own field or national programme and may call for recusal on those ballots; he has no apparent connection to Katori or Ye.

Kroll discloses a year in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder during his PhD; Jun Ye is at JILA in the same community. He reports no direct collaboration or supervision with Katori or Ye and does not consider it recusal-level, but the committee should note it because Kroll prefers B042.

Olsson discloses that B028 is in her own field (transmission electron microscopy) and that she knows the aberration-correction community, but sees no direct tie to Rose, Urban or Haider; she has moved away from B028.

Lindroth discloses a long-time collaboration with 2023 laureate Anne L'Huillier, not a connection to any shortlisted candidate, and flags that as an atomic theorist she may overvalue precision metrology.
Pearce (chair) reports no tie to any credited person; his field is close to B032 and B057, and he flags his opening ranking of B032 as a possible taste bias.

Danielsson (Secretary) reports no apparent conflict with any shortlisted candidate and says he will separate the commissioning of outside evaluations from advocacy. Eriksson and Mehlig report no apparent conflicts.
questions_for_round2: For B042, does anyone beyond Katori and Ye (Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto, Hinkley, Bloom) have a priority claim on the first lattice-clock demonstrations that would change the pair, and can Ye's contribution be worded as realisation at record accuracy without re-crediting the 2005 comb prize?

Does the committee accept optical lattice clocks as a discovery or invention that satisfies the will, given that frequency combs (2005) and ion control (2012) have been recognised, and should the citation avoid reference to the redefinition of the second?

For B019, are the open pairing mechanism and the eight-year age a reason to wait, or is a citation limited to the flat-band prediction and the observed correlated insulating and superconducting phases acceptable? What in the mechanism could change in the next few years?

For B019, can the omission of Yuan Cao and other early experimental groups, and the earlier Lopes dos Santos twist-angle theory, be handled in the citation wording, or does it require different names?
Between B042 and B019, which can each member support if the other does not prevail, given that Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson and Johansson already name the other as a fall-back?

For B032, do the expert reports say whether Spiering's Baikal and DUMAND-era role is as decisive as Halzen's relative to the AMANDA, DUMAND and ANTARES pioneers, and does the diffuse flux alone justify a citation while sources are at 3-4 sigma?
For B057, can a three-person ATLAS and CMS attribution be defined that the experimental communities accept, and would a detector-centred citation be acceptable? Which of the three names is weakest?

Should the committee consider a two-part prize pairing B019 or B042 with another candidate, or keep single-achievement prizes only, and should the AMO cluster (B042, B050, B038, B049) be treated as one competing group given recent prizes?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows two leading configurations and one minority: B042 (four explicit supporters), B019 (three) and B032 (one). Danielsson, Johansson, Olsson, Mehlig and Pearce changed their first choice after the openings, in each case toward B042, B019 or B032. B042 is the most frequently named alternative among members who prefer other candidates. The open issues are the discovery-versus-metrology reading and possible priority claims for B042, and the maturity, pairing-mechanism and credit questions for B019. All counts are limited to positions stated in the eight round-1 files.
